newsitem.title: PERU: Peru replaces officials held hostage by guerrillas.
newsitem.headline: Peru replaces officials held hostage by guerrillas.

text.p: President Alberto Fujimori replaced Peru's top security officials and the president of the country's Supreme Court, who are all being held hostage by Marxist guerrillas, the Interior Ministry said on Thursday.
The chief of the anti-terrorist police DINCOTE, Gen. Maximo Rivera, was replaced by Gen. Marcel Nakamura.
The country's security chief, Gen. Guillermo Bobbio Zevallos, was replaced by Gen. Arturo Marquina.
Supreme Court President Moises Pantoja was replaced by Victor Raul Castillo, who was sworn in by Fujimori at the Palace of Justice. Pantoja's term ended on Dec. 31.

The security chiefs were under fire for lowering their guard in the fight against Peru's guerrillas and allowing the Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement to storm the Japanese ambassador's residence on Dec. 17 and seize 500 hostages.
Sixteen days later, the guerrillas still held 74 captives, including top Peruvian officials, foreign diplomats, Japanese VIPs and Fujimori's younger brother, Pedro.
The rebels are using the hostages as bargaining chips to demand the release from jail of over 400 of their comrades.
